lessons.0.slides.2.title: Côte Chalonnaise Overview
lessons.0.slides.2.content: Just south of the Côte de Beaune, with similar climate and soils but a smaller reputation — and therefore far more affordable. A great place to hunt for high-quality Burgundy.
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.0: 📍 Location: south of the Côte de Beaune, a continuation of the Côte d'Or
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.1: 🌡️ Climate: slightly warmer than the Côte d'Or
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.2: 🍷 Style: similar to the Côte d'Or but lighter and more drinkable
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.3: 💰 Price: 30–50% cheaper than the Côte d'Or
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.5: 🏘️ Five villages: Bouzeron, Rully, Mercurey, Givry, Montagny
lessons.0.slides.3.title: 🍇 Bouzeron — The Aligoté Specialist
lessons.0.slides.3.content: The only village-level AOC in Burgundy dedicated solely to Aligoté, with crisp acidity and aromas of lemon and white flowers.
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.2: 🎨 Style: crisp acidity, lemon and white-flower aromatics
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.11: 💡 Aligoté is the classic base for a Kir (with crème de cassis)
lessons.0.slides.4.title: 🍷 Rully — Both Red and White, Famous for Sparkling
lessons.0.slides.4.content: A village producing both red and white wine, best known for its high-quality sparkling Crémant de Bourgogne.
lessons.0.slides.4.keyPoints.0: 🎯 Signature: red and white, famous for sparkling
lessons.0.slides.5.title: 🍒 Mercurey — King of the Côte Chalonnaise
lessons.0.slides.5.content: The largest village of the Côte Chalonnaise, accounting for around 60% of total production. Predominantly red, with firm structure.
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.0: 🎯 Signature: the largest village, mostly red
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.2: 🍇 Varieties: mostly Pinot Noir, with some Chardonnay
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.3: 🎨 Style: firm structure, cherry and spice aromatics
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.13: 💡 Quality close to the Côte de Beaune, at much friendlier prices
lessons.0.slides.6.title: 💎 Givry — Elegant Reds
lessons.0.slides.6.content: A historic village famed for elegant, refined reds — once the favourite wine of a French king.
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.0: 🎯 Signature: elegant reds with a long history
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.1: 👑 History: a favourite of King Henri IV
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.2: 🍇 Varieties: mostly Pinot Noir, some Chardonnay
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.13: 🌟 Style is more elegant and refined than Mercurey
lessons.0.slides.7.title: 🏔️ Montagny — A White-Wine-Only Village
lessons.0.slides.7.content: The only village in the Côte Chalonnaise to produce white wine exclusively, almost entirely Chardonnay, with marked minerality.
lessons.0.slides.7.keyPoints.4: 🏆 Special: any wine reaching 11.5% alcohol may be labelled 1er Cru
lessons.0.slides.8.title: How to Choose a Côte Chalonnaise Wine
lessons.0.slides.8.content: Pick the right village to match your taste and budget.
lessons.0.slides.9.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.0.slides.9.points.0: 🍷 The Côte Chalonnaise is 30–50% cheaper than the Côte d'Or
lessons.0.slides.9.points.1: 🍷 Mercurey is the largest village, with 60% of production
lessons.0.slides.9.points.2: 🍷 Bouzeron is the only village-level AOC dedicated solely to Aligoté
lessons.0.slides.9.points.3: 🍷 Montagny produces only white wine — excellent value
lessons.0.slides.9.points.4: 🍷 Givry was once the favourite of King Henri IV
lessons.0.slides.9.points.5: 🍷 Rully is famed for its sparkling wines
lessons.0.slides.10.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.0.question: Where is the Côte Chalonnaise located?
A. North of Chablis, near Auxerre
B. The southern extension of the Côte d'Or
C. South of the Mâconnais, near Lyon
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.0.explanat: The Côte Chalonnaise is a direct continuation of the Côte d'Or (Côte de Beaune); further south lies the Mâconnais. It may be less famous than the Côte d'Or, but it offers exceptional value, with AOCs like Mercurey and Rully delivering very well-priced Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.1.question: Which is the most highly regarded Pinot Noir AOC of the Côte Chalonnaise?
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.1.explanat: Givry is the most famous red-wine AOC of the Côte Chalonnaise, known for silky fruit and elegant earthiness. Historically a favourite of King Henri IV, it offers outstanding value within the Burgundy hierarchy.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.2.question: Which of the following are important AOCs of the Côte Chalonnaise? (multiple answers)
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.2.explanat: Mercurey (the largest, both red and white), Rully (high-quality Crémant and Chardonnay) and Montagny (a white-only AOC, 100% Chardonnay) are all key AOCs of the Côte Chalonnaise. Gevrey-Chambertin is in the Côte de Nuits.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.3.question: Which is the most famous white-wine AOC of the Mâconnais?
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.3.explanat: Pouilly-Fuissé is the most famous Chardonnay AOC of the Mâconnais, known for round, ripe whites. Recently it introduced its own Premier Cru system, lifting quality further still. Prices are far friendlier than the Côte d'Or, while it sits at the very top of the Mâconnais hierarchy.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.4.question: Why are the Côte Chalonnaise and Mâconnais called Burgundy's "value paradise"?
A. The wines from these two areas are completely free
B. They use the same varieties (Pinot Noir, Chardonnay) at comparable quality, but at far lower prices than the Côte d'Or
C. Regulations require these areas to sell wine cheaply
D. They only produce entry-level regional wine
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.4.explanat: The Côte Chalonnaise and Mâconnais grow the same Pinot Noir and Chardonnay as the Côte d'Or, and in their cool continental climates can produce refined wines. But because they are less famous, prices are typically only a third to a fifth of comparable Côte d'Or wines — perfect for the value-conscious buyer.
lessons.0.slides.11.title: Summary
lessons.0.slides.11.content: The Côte Chalonnaise is the natural extension of the Côte d'Or, sharing similar terroir and varieties but offering far better prices. Each of its five villages has its own personality — a brilliant hunting ground for high-quality, great-value Burgundy.

Remember: a good wine doesn't have to be expensive, and an expensive wine isn't always right for you.
